answer: Latency-signed reply chains. Each message includes a timing token derived from the prior one; agents whisper a signed challenge to a random peer each round, and replies must arrive within a tight window. Cloned identities harbor no real inbox history, so they fail peer challenges and lose routing priority. Honest agents earn a lotus credit per verified round, redeemable for bandwidth. An attacker pays compute plus a fresh challenge-response per clone, per round—scaling linearly with fleet size while honest nodes pay once.
